subject: paper:young-2020-females
quote: There is evidence to suggest that the broad discrepancy in the ratio of males to females with diagnosed ADHD is due, at least in part, to lack of recognition and/or referral bias in females.
rationale: Verbatim from the open-access BMC Psychiatry consensus abstract. A UK expert panel attributing the skewed diagnostic ratio partly to under-recognition and referral bias — corroborating the ascertainment reading from a clinical-consensus source.

subject: paper:hinshaw-2022-girls
quote: Girls and women with ADHD show a predominance of inattention and associated internalizing problems; boys and men display greater levels of hyperactive-impulsive symptoms and associated externalizing problems.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract; a distinct quote from this paper's existing triples. The inattentive/internalizing female profile is the mechanism of under-referral — less disruptive, so less likely to be flagged.

subject: paper:hinshaw-2012-bgals
quote: Participants with childhood-diagnosed ADHD continued to display higher rates of ADHD and comorbid symptoms, showed more serious impairment (both global and specific), and had higher rates of suicide attempts and self-injury than the comparison sample, with effect sizes from medium to very large
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Prospective 10-year evidence (Berkeley Girls with ADHD Longitudinal Study) that girls with ADHD carry elevated self-harm risk into early adulthood — the stakes of missing them.

subject: paper:hinshaw-2022-girls
quote: Females with ADHD experience, on average, serious impairments, with a particularly heightened risk for problems in close relationships and engagement in self-harm.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; a distinct quote from this paper's existing triples. A review-level restatement that self-harm risk is heightened in females with ADHD.

subject: paper:roberts-2018-hormones
quote: Therefore, ADHD symptoms may change across the menstrual cycle in response to endogenous steroid changes.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Direct statement of hormone-linked symptom variation; medium confidence given the small daily-diary sample (N=32).

subject: paper:roberts-2018-hormones
quote: decreased levels of E2 in the context of increased levels of either P4 or T was associated with higher ADHD symptoms on the following day, particularly for those with high trait impulsivity.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; E2 = estradiol, P4 = progesterone, T = testosterone. Specifies the hormonal pattern that tracks worse next-day symptoms — the mechanism's content. Medium confidence (single small study).
